newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's UNITA pledges to help keep peace on track.
newsitem.headline: Angola's UNITA pledges to help keep peace on track.

text.p: Angola's UNITA opposition promised on Thursday to fulfil new commitments within 10 days to make progress on political and military issues that are stalling the country's peace process.

The U.N. special envoy to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, met UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi on Thursday in his stronghold of Bailundo and returned to the capital Luanda saying he had received fresh promises from UNITA's leadership.
"Within the next 10 days UNITA wants to resolve all military and political issues," Beye told a news conference.

He said UNITA would begin sending its top generals to Luanda before September 20 for integration into a single national army and would hand in heavy weapons in all remaining areas under its control including diamond-rich regions.
Beye said Savimbi had also called for a meeting with President Jose Eduardo dos Santos to discuss political issues before September 20.
A delegation from the MPLA-led government will travel to Bailundo for talks with Savimbi on Friday.

A two-year-old peace deal between the two groups which fought a bitter civil war for 20 years hit rocky ground last month when Savimbi turned down an offer of the vice-presidency in a unity government.
MPLA leaders increased the tension this week by saying if Savimbi won't take the job, he should not be allowed to send a substitute instead.
Beye has expressed concern that there has been no progress in the peace process for two months.
The U.N. peacekeeping force is expected to withdraw its soldiers as scheduled next February.
